cta: Machine or pilot: who should get the last word? Comment

facts.label: Day of February of the crash
Airspeed when the stick shaker fired and the autopilot disengaged, knots
People aboard who were killed (2 pilots, 2 flight attendants, 45 passengers)

thumbnail.pattern: the niche's air-crash covers show the airliner itself big at the moment it goes wrong with a few bold words; ours shows our blueprint cutaway of the nose with the column straining forward and the pusher glowing red under the floor

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Colgan Air's plane could push its own nose down.

params.place: beside the twin-propeller airliner in the snowy night cloud near Buffalo, its wing already tinted amber

moments.what: the airliner side-on in the snow, gear down, wing tinted amber, date caption and reconstruction tag, COLGAN AIR types on, the airspeed plate
the propellers blur, snow streaks past the wing
push in on the nose as it dips by itself, STICK PUSHER: NOSE DOWN types on in green
the nose comes back up a little

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So why didn't it save the plane? The control column shakes first, as a warning. If the wing gets close to losing its lift, a machine shoves the column forward.

params.place: close along the airliner's fuselage past the lit cockpit windows to its high wing, in the snowy cloud

moments.what: close on the lit cockpit windows, WHY DIDN'T IT WORK? types on
the camera drifts along the nose past the cockpit
the airliner trembles, FIRST: COLUMN SHAKES types on in amber
the amber tint on the wing deepens
the camera slides out to the high wing, glowing amber toward red
WING NEAR A STALL types on in red
THEN: PUSHER types on in green, the trembling stops
pull wide: the whole airliner lowers its nose, NOSE DOWN

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Near Buffalo, in February {fact1}, the shaker fired at {fact3} knots. Then the pusher fired. So why did the nose come back up?

params.place: below the approach path to Buffalo at night, looking up through the snow at the airliner passing over the runway's approach lights

moments.what: the approach lights in the snow, the airliner's landing lights above, NEAR BUFFALO types on
the date tag types on
the camera tilts up to the airliner, its data tag turns amber: SHAKER
the airspeed on its data tag glows amber as the figure is said
the airliner's nose wobbles, the wing tinting amber
push in: PUSHER FIRED: NOSE DOWN types on in green and the nose dips
the nose rises again, a red question mark on the data tag

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But the captain dragged the column back against it. It fired twice more, and he pulled back each time.

params.place: back in the cutaway, close on the captain's hands and the column, the pusher's rod under the floor

moments.what: the column is shoved forward, a green PUSH arrow and the pusher lamp lit, CAPTAIN pinned to the hands on the yoke
the hands drag the column back, a red PULL arrow strikes the green one, a red flash
the pusher's rod strains under the floor, glowing red
pull out: the pusher lamps light two more times, the column lunges
each time the hands drag it back, OVERRIDDEN stamps on

params.place: beneath the wing in the cloud, looking up at its underside, time slowed

moments.what: silence: the wing's underside fills the frame glowing red, snow streaking past
the sub-boom: the wing drops away, THE WING STALLS
wide: the airliner rolls onto its side in the cloud

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The airliner rolled hard onto its right side, dived, and hit a house. All {fact4} aboard were killed, and {fact5} on the ground.

place: side-on beside the airliner as it rolls onto its side and dives
over the snowy rooftops of Clarence Center at night
down on the snowy street where fire engines and firefighters arrive

moments.what: side-on: the airliner rolls onto its right side, ONTO ITS SIDE, DIVING types on in red
its nose drops into the cloud
cut far above the snowy town: an orange glow rises between the houses, CLARENCE CENTER
the toll plate for the people aboard lands
down into the street: fire engines' lights flash, firefighters with lamps walk toward the glow
the second plate, for the person on the ground, lands below

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Machine or pilot: who gets the last word? Full story on our channel.

params.place: beside the airliner in the snowy cloud again, quiet before the warning

moments.what: the airliner flying level in the snow, MACHINE types on
OR PILOT? types on
the camera drifts in toward the airliner
FULL STORY ON THE CHANNEL types on, the wing tints amber again, back to the first frame
